newsitem.title: USA: Alabama highway bonds go to House Ways and Means.
newsitem.headline: Alabama highway bonds go to House Ways and Means.

text.p: Alabama Gov. Fob James' $700 million highway bond proposal was scheduled to go before the House Ways and Means Committee on Wednesday, though it was unclear when the panel would vote on the controversial plan.
Lawmakers expect "a lot of discussion" on the proposal, an aide to the committee said Tuesday.
The bill advanced earlier this month from the Joint Highway Committee despite complaints from urban lawmakers who said their districts were shortchanged.

James plan would use existing gasoline taxes to pay debt service on the 20-year bonds. It allocates $150 million for resurfacing roads and highways, $150 million for bridge repair and replacements and $81.9 million to be divided among the state's 67 counties for local projects.
The remaining $318 million would fund contruction of bypasses around Birmingham, Huntsville, Tuscaloosa, Decatur, Montgomery and Anniston, plus widening of several two-lane highways to four lanes.
If approved by the Ways and Means Committee, the bill would then go to the full House for a vote.
